placementGuidelines: Heavy-feeding repeat bloomer that does best with morning sun (dries dew off leaves fast, reducing fungal disease like black spot) and afternoon shade tolerance. Use the 'five-leaf-leaflet' deadheading trick to force new blooms without a painful full structural prune: follow a faded bloom's stem down to the first cluster with 5 leaflets (not 3) and snip 1/4 in. above it - the plant will not push flowers from a 3-leaf node. Cheap leather welding gloves (rather than pricier gardening gloves) give full forearm thorn protection for low-effort maintenance pruning. In-ground roses can take a stronger phosphorus-heavy bloom-booster dose than potted plants (e.g., 2 tbsp per 2 gal. water poured around the drip line) once every 4 weeks through summer; always water plain first and keep the liquid off leaves/petals to avoid scorch and fungal issues. Pairs well underplanted with volunteer Mexican Petunia and self-seeding Rose Campion for a low-cost cottage-garden bed.
